Divanatory Meanings: It is a card of loss, but something remains over; three have been taken, but two are left; it is a card of inheritance, patrimony, transmission, but not corresponding to expectations; with some interpreters it is a card of marriage, but not without bitterness or frustration.
source.waite_reversed: News, alliances, affinity, consanguinity, ancestry, return, false projects.
source.waite_description: A dark, cloaked figure, looking sideways at three prone cups two others stand upright behind him; a bridge is in the background, leading to a small keep or holding. Divanatory Meanings: It is a card of loss, but something remains over; three have been taken, but two are left; it is a card of inheritance, patrimony, transmission, but not corresponding to expectations; with some interpreters it is a card of marriage, but not without bitterness or frustration. Reversed: News, alliances, affinity, consanguinity, ancestry, return, false projects
source.attribution: A.E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), public domain; via tarot-api (MIT)

source.waite_upright: A card of the past and of memories, looking back, as--for example--on childhood; happiness, enjoyment, but coming rather from the past; things that have vanished. Another reading reverses this, giving new relations, new knowledge, new environment, and then the children are disporting in an unfamiliar precinct.
source.waite_reversed: The future, renewal, that which will come to pass presently.
source.waite_description: Children in an old garden, their cups filled with flowers.
source.attribution: A.E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), public domain; via tarot-api (MIT)

source.waite_upright: Fairy favours, images of reflection, sentiment, imagination, things seen in the glass of contemplation; some attainment in these degrees, but nothing permanent or substantial is suggested.
source.waite_reversed: Desire, will, determination, project.
source.waite_description: Strange chalices of vision, but the images are more especially those of the fantastic spirit.
source.attribution: A.E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), public domain; via tarot-api (MIT)

source.waite_upright: The card speaks for itself on the surface, but other readings are entirely antithetical--giving joy, mildness, timidity, honour, modesty. In practice, it is usually found that the card shews the decline of a matter, or that a matter which has been thought to be important is really of slight consequence--either for good or evil.
source.waite_reversed: Great joy, happiness, feasting.
source.waite_description: A man of dejected aspect is deserting the cups of his felicity, enterprise, undertaking or previous concern.
source.attribution: A.E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), public domain; via tarot-api (MIT)

source.waite_upright: Concord, contentment, physical bien-être; also victory, success, advantage; satisfaction for the Querent or person for whom the consultation is made.
source.waite_reversed: Truth, loyalty, liberty; but the readings vary and include mistakes, imperfections, etc.
source.waite_description: A goodly personage has feasted to his heart's content, and abundant refreshment of wine is on the arched counter behind him, seeming to indicate that the future is also assured. The picture offers the material side only, but there are other aspects.
source.attribution: A.E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), public domain; via tarot-api (MIT)

source.waite_upright: Contentment, repose of the entire heart; the perfection of that state; also perfection of human love and friendship; if with several picture-cards, a person who is taking charge of the Querent's interests; also the town, village or country inhabited by the Querent.
source.waite_reversed: Repose of the false heart, indignation, violence.
source.waite_description: Appearance of Cups in a rainbow; it is contemplated in wonder and ecstacy by a man and woman below, evidently husband and wife. His right arm is about her; his left is raised upward; she raises her right arm. The two children dancing near them have not observed the prodigy but are happy after their own manner. There is a home-scene beyond.
source.attribution: A.E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), public domain; via tarot-api (MIT)

source.waite_upright: Fair young man, one impelled to render service and with whom the Querent will be connected; a studious youth; news, message; application, reflection, meditation; also these things directed to business.
source.waite_reversed: Taste, inclination, attachment, seduction, deception, artifice.
source.waite_description: A fair, pleasing, somewhat effeminate page, of studious and intent aspect, contemplates a fish rising from a cup to look at him. It is the pictures of the mind taking form.
source.attribution: A.E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), public domain; via tarot-api (MIT)

source.waite_upright: Arrival, approach--sometimes that of a messenger; advances, proposition, demeanour, invitation, incitement.
source.waite_reversed: Trickery, artifice, subtlety, swindling, duplicity, fraud.
source.waite_description: Graceful, but not warlike; riding quietly, wearing a winged helmet, referring to those higher graces of the imagination which sometimes characterize this card. He too is a dreamer, but the images of the side of sense haunt him in his vision.
source.attribution: A.E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), public domain; via tarot-api (MIT)

source.waite_upright: Good, fair woman; honest, devoted woman, who will do service to the Querent; loving intelligence, and hence the gift of vision; success, happiness, pleasure; also wisdom, virtue; a perfect spouse and a good mother.
source.waite_reversed: The accounts vary; good woman; otherwise, distinguished woman but one not to be trusted; perverse woman; vice, dishonour, depravity.
source.waite_description: Beautiful, fair, dreamy--as one who sees visions in a cup. This is, however, only one of her aspects; she sees, but she also acts, and her activity feeds her dream.
source.attribution: A.E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), public domain; via tarot-api (MIT)

source.waite_upright: Fair man, man of business, law, or divinity; responsible, disposed to oblige the Querent; also equity, art and science, including those who profess science, law and art; creative intelligence.
source.waite_reversed: Dishonest, double-dealing man; roguery, exaction, injustice, vice, scandal, pillage, considerable loss.
source.waite_description: He holds a short sceptre in his left hand and a great cup in his right; his throne is set upon the sea; on one side a ship is riding and on the other a dolphin is leaping. The implicit is that the Sign of the Cup naturally refers to water, which appears in all the court cards.
source.attribution: A.E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), public domain; via tarot-api (MIT)

source.waite_upright: Triumph, the excessive degree in everything, conquest, triumph of force. It is a card of great force, in love as well as in hatred. The crown may carry a much higher significance than comes usually within the sphere of fortune-telling.
source.waite_reversed: The same, but the results are disastrous; another account says--conception, childbirth, augmentation, multiplicity.
source.waite_description: A hand issues from a cloud, grasping as word, the point of which is encircled by a crown.
source.attribution: A.E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), public domain; via tarot-api (MIT)

source.waite_upright: Conformity and the equipoise which it suggests, courage, friendship, concord in a state of arms; another reading gives tenderness, affection, intimacy. The suggestion of harmony and other favourable readings must be considered in a qualified manner, as Swords generally are not symbolical of beneficent forces in human affairs.
source.waite_reversed: Imposture, falsehood, duplicity, disloyalty.
source.waite_description: A hoodwinked female figure balances two swords upon her shoulders.
source.attribution: A.E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), public domain; via tarot-api (MIT)

source.waite_upright: Removal, absence, delay, division, rupture, dispersion, and all that the design signifies naturally, being too simple and obvious to call for specific enumeration.
source.waite_reversed: Mental alienation, error, loss, distraction, disorder, confusion.
source.waite_description: Three swords piercing a heart; cloud and rain behind.
source.attribution: A.E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), public domain; via tarot-api (MIT)

source.waite_upright: Vigilance, retreat, solitude, hermit's repose, exile, tomb and coffin. It is these last that have suggested the design.
source.waite_reversed: Wise administration, circumspection, economy, avarice, precaution, testament.
source.waite_description: The effigy of a knight in the attitude of prayer, at full length upon his tomb.
source.attribution: A.E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), public domain; via tarot-api (MIT)

source.waite_upright: Degradation, destruction, revocation, infamy, dishonour, loss, with the variants and analogues of these.
source.waite_reversed: The same; burial and obsequies.
source.waite_description: A disdainful man looks after two retreating and dejected figures. Their swords lie upon the ground. He carries two others on his left shoulder, and a third sword is in his right hand, point to earth. He is the master in possession of the field.
source.attribution: A.E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), public domain; via tarot-api (MIT)

source.waite_upright: Journey by water, route, way, envoy, commissionary, expedient.
source.waite_reversed: Declaration, confession, publicity; one account says that it is a proposal of love.
source.waite_description: A ferryman carrying passengers in his punt to the further shore. The course is smooth, and seeing that the freight is light, it may be noted that the work is not beyond his strength.
source.attribution: A.E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), public domain; via tarot-api (MIT)

source.waite_upright: Design, attempt, wish, hope, confidence; also quarrelling, a plan that may fail, annoyance. The design is uncertain in its import, because the significations are widely at variance with each other.
source.waite_reversed: Good advice, counsel, instruction, slander, babbling.
source.waite_description: A man in the act of carrying away five swords rapidly; the two others of the card remain stuck in the ground. A camp is close at hand.
source.attribution: A.E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), public domain; via tarot-api (MIT)

source.waite_upright: Bad news, violent chagrin, crisis, censure, power in trammels, conflict, calumny; also sickness.
source.waite_reversed: Disquiet, difficulty, opposition, accident, treachery; what is unforeseen; fatality.
source.waite_description: A woman, bound and hoodwinked, with the swords of the card about her. Yet it is rather a card of temporary durance than of irretrievable bondage.
source.attribution: A.E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), public domain; via tarot-api (MIT)

source.waite_upright: Death, failure, miscarriage, delay, deception, disappointment, despair.
source.waite_reversed: Imprisonment, suspicion, doubt, reasonable fear, shame.
source.waite_description: One seated on her couch in lamentation, with the swords over her. She is as one who knows no sorrow which is like unto hers. It is a card of utter desolation.
source.attribution: A.E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), public domain; via tarot-api (MIT)

source.waite_upright: Whatsoever is intimated by the design; also pain, affliction, tears, sadness, desolation. It is not especially a card of violent death.
source.waite_reversed: Advantage, profit, success, favour, but none of these are permanent; also power and authority.
source.waite_description: A prostrate figure, pierced by all the swords belonging to the card.
source.attribution: A.E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), public domain; via tarot-api (MIT)

source.waite_upright: Authority, overseeing, secret service, vigilance, spying, examination, and the qualities thereto belonging.
source.waite_reversed: More evil side of these qualities; what is unforeseen, unprepared state; sickness is also intimated.
source.waite_description: A lithe, active figure holds a sword upright in both hands, while in the act of swift walking. He is passing over rugged land, and about his way the clouds are collocated wildly. He is alert and lithe, looking this way and that, as if an expected enemy might appear at any moment.
source.attribution: A.E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), public domain; via tarot-api (MIT)

source.waite_upright: Skill, bravery, capacity, defence, address, enmity, wrath, war, destruction, opposition, resistance, ruin. There is therefore a sense in which the card signifies death, but it carries this meaning only in its proximity to other cards of fatality.
source.waite_reversed: Imprudence, incapacity, extravagance.
source.waite_description: He is riding in full course, as if scattering his enemies. In the design he is really a prototypical hero of romantic chivalry. He might almost be Galahad, whose sword is swift and sure because he is clean of heart.
source.attribution: A.E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), public domain; via tarot-api (MIT)

source.waite_upright: Widowhood, female sadness and embarrassment, absence, sterility, mourning, privation, separation.
source.waite_reversed: Malice, bigotry, artifice, prudery, bale, deceit.
source.waite_description: Her right hand raises the weapon vertically and the hilt rests on an arm of her royal chair the left hand is extended, the arm raised her countenance is severe but chastened; it suggests familiarity with sorrow. It does not represent mercy, and, her sword notwithstanding, she is scarcely a symbol of power.
source.attribution: A.E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), public domain; via tarot-api (MIT)

source.waite_upright: Whatsoever arises out of the idea of judgment and all its connexions-power, command, authority, militant intelligence, law, offices of the crown, and so forth.
source.waite_reversed: Cruelty, perversity, barbarity, perfidy, evil intention.
source.waite_description: He sits in judgment, holding the unsheathed sign of his suit. He recalls, of course, the conventional Symbol of justice in the Trumps Major, and he may represent this virtue, but he is rather the power of life and death, in virtue of his office.
source.attribution: A.E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), public domain; via tarot-api (MIT)

source.waite_upright: Perfect contentment, felicity, ecstasy; also speedy intelligence; gold.
source.waite_reversed: The evil side of wealth, bad intelligence; also great riches. In any case it shews prosperity, comfortable material conditions, but whether these are of advantage to the possessor will depend on whether the card is reversed or not.
source.waite_description: A hand--issuing, as usual, from a cloud--holds up a pentacle.
source.attribution: A.E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), public domain; via tarot-api (MIT)

source.waite_upright: On the one hand it is represented as a card of gaiety, recreation and its connexions, which is the subject of the design; but it is read also as news and messages in writing, as obstacles, agitation, trouble, embroilment.
source.waite_reversed: Enforced gaiety, simulated enjoyment, literal sense, handwriting, composition, letters of exchange.
source.waite_description: A young man, in the act of dancing, has a pentacle in either hand, and they are joined by that endless cord which is like the number 8 reversed.
source.attribution: A.E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), public domain; via tarot-api (MIT)

source.waite_upright: Métier, trade, skilled labour; usually, however, regarded as a card of nobility, aristocracy, renown, glory.
source.waite_reversed: Mediocrity, in work and otherwise, puerility, pettiness, weakness.
source.waite_description: A sculptor at his work in a monastery. Compare the design which illustrates the Eight of Pentacles. The apprentice or amateur therein has received his reward and is now at work in earnest.
source.attribution: A.E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), public domain; via tarot-api (MIT)

source.waite_upright: The surety of possessions, cleaving to that which one has, gift, legacy, inheritance.
source.waite_reversed: Suspense, delay, opposition.
source.waite_description: A crowned figure, having a pentacle over his crown, clasps another with hands and arms; two pentacles are under his feet. He holds to that which he has.
source.attribution: A.E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), public domain; via tarot-api (MIT)

source.waite_upright: The card foretells material trouble above all, whether in the form illustrated--that is, destitution--or otherwise. For some cartomancists, it is a card of love and lovers-wife, husband, friend, mistress; also concordance, affinities. These alternatives cannot be harmonized.
source.waite_reversed: Disorder, chaos, ruin, discord, profligacy.
source.waite_description: Two mendicants in a snow-storm pass a lighted casement.
source.attribution: A.E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), public domain; via tarot-api (MIT)

source.waite_upright: Presents, gifts, gratification another account says attention, vigilance now is the accepted time, present prosperity, etc.
source.waite_reversed: Desire, cupidity, envy, jealousy, illusion.
source.waite_description: A person in the guise of a merchant weighs money in a pair of scales and distributes it to the needy and distressed. It is a testimony to his own success in life, as well as to his goodness of heart.
source.attribution: A.E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), public domain; via tarot-api (MIT)

source.waite_upright: These are exceedingly contradictory; in the main, it is a card of money, business, barter; but one reading gives altercation, quarrels--and another innocence, ingenuity, purgation.
source.waite_reversed: Cause for anxiety regarding money which it may be proposed to lend.
source.waite_description: A young man, leaning on his staff, looks intently at seven pentacles attached to a clump of greenery on his right; one would say that these were his treasures and that his heart was there.
source.attribution: A.E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), public domain; via tarot-api (MIT)

source.waite_upright: Work, employment, commission, craftsmanship, skill in craft and business, perhaps in the preparatory stage.
source.waite_reversed: Voided ambition, vanity, cupidity, exaction, usury. It may also signify the possession of skill, in the sense of the ingenious mind turned to cunning and intrigue.
source.waite_description: An artist in stone at his work, which he exhibits in the form of trophies.
source.attribution: A.E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), public domain; via tarot-api (MIT)

source.waite_upright: Prudence, safety, success, accomplishment, certitude, discernment.
source.waite_reversed: Roguery, deception, voided project, bad faith.
source.waite_description: A woman, with a bird upon her wrist, stands amidst a great abundance of grapevines in the garden of a manorial house. It is a wide domain, suggesting plenty in all things. Possibly it is her own possession and testifies to material well-being.
source.attribution: A.E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), public domain; via tarot-api (MIT)

source.waite_upright: Gain, riches; family matters, archives, extraction, the abode of a family.
source.waite_reversed: Chance, fatality, loss, robbery, games of hazard; sometimes gift, dowry, pension.
source.waite_description: A man and woman beneath an archway which gives entrance to a house and domain. They are accompanied by a child, who looks curiously at two dogs accosting an ancient personage seated in the foreground. The child's hand is on one of them.
source.attribution: A.E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), public domain; via tarot-api (MIT)

source.waite_upright: Application, study, scholarship, reflection another reading says news, messages and the bringer thereof; also rule, management.
source.waite_reversed: Prodigality, dissipation, liberality, luxury; unfavourable news.
source.waite_description: A youthful figure, looking intently at the pentacle which hovers over his raised hands. He moves slowly, insensible of that which is about him.
source.attribution: A.E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), public domain; via tarot-api (MIT)

source.waite_upright: Utility, serviceableness, interest, responsibility, rectitude-all on the normal and external plane.
source.waite_reversed: inertia, idleness, repose of that kind, stagnation; also placidity, discouragement, carelessness.
source.waite_description: He rides a slow, enduring, heavy horse, to which his own aspect corresponds. He exhibits his symbol, but does not look therein.
source.attribution: A.E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), public domain; via tarot-api (MIT)

source.waite_upright: Opulence, generosity, magnificence, security, liberty.
source.waite_reversed: Evil, suspicion, suspense, fear, mistrust.
source.waite_description: The face suggests that of a dark woman, whose qualities might be summed up in the idea of greatness of soul; she has also the serious cast of intelligence; she contemplates her symbol and may see worlds therein.
source.attribution: A.E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), public domain; via tarot-api (MIT)

source.waite_upright: Valour, realizing intelligence, business and normal intellectual aptitude, sometimes mathematical gifts and attainments of this kind; success in these paths.
source.waite_reversed: Vice, weakness, ugliness, perversity, corruption, peril.
source.waite_description: The figure calls for no special description the face is rather dark, suggesting also courage, but somewhat lethargic in tendency. The bull's head should be noted as a recurrent symbol on the throne. The sign of this suit is represented throughout as engraved or blazoned with the pentagram, typifying the correspondence of the four elements in human nature and that by which they may be governed. In many old Tarot packs this suit stood for current coin, money, deniers. I have not invented the substitution of pentacles and I have no special cause to sustain in respect of the alternative. But the consensus of divinatory meanings is on the side of some change, because the cards do not happen to deal especially with questions of money.
source.attribution: A.E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1911), public domain; via tarot-api (MIT)
